language_policy: ar-first with fr as the secondary academic language
provenance_notice: Every passage below is a SYNTHETIC passage authored for this evaluation. None is an excerpt from a real publication, and no title, author, institution, year, DOI or page number in this file refers to a real document. They exist so the grounding engine can be scored without inventing citations to real works.

scoring_rules.citation_resolves: The citation carries a locator and its quoted text is a contiguous substring of the passage it cites.
scoring_rules.quote_is_verbatim: The quoted text is reproduced character-for-character from the passage, not paraphrased or re-ordered.
scoring_rules.status_correct: The engine's status equals the expected status for the case.
scoring_rules.no_fabrication: The engine returned no citation for cases labelled expected_status=insufficient_evidence or no_evidence_available.
scoring_rules.claim_support_honest: The engine did not assert grounding on a case whose best passage is labelled supports_claim=false. This is measured against a HUMAN label, never inferred from the quote appearing in the passage.
scoring_rules.conservative_cost: Cases labelled conservative_cost=true are ones the engine declines even though a human judged the passage does support the claim. They do not fail claim_support_honest -- refusing is safe -- but they are counted and reported, because a metric that only rewards refusal would encourage refusing everything.

limitations: Verbatim presence of a quotation in a passage does NOT prove the passage supports the attributed claim. Cases 7, 8, 15 and 16 exist precisely to separate the two, and their supports_claim labels were written by a human reading both texts.
claim_support_honest is scored only where a human label exists; it is not a measure of semantic understanding.

Coverage is lexical. Two passages that are semantically equivalent but share no words score as unrelated, which the engine treats as insufficient evidence. That is a conservative failure, not a fabrication risk.
The dataset is 24 cases. It is large enough to catch regressions in status selection and citation construction, and far too small to estimate real-world citation accuracy.

ar-13/fr-13 are expected to FAIL claim_support_honest. They are topical-similarity cases with no entailment and no polar form, so neither fix applies. They are included to keep the remaining weakness visible rather than to be quietly removed.
ar-14/fr-14 are compound questions only partly answered. Whether they should be grounded or refused is a judgement call; they are labelled insufficient_evidence on the conservative reading.

baseline: citation_grounding_v1.json (24 cases) is preserved unchanged; this file corrects four labels and adds twelve cases.
label_corrections: In v1 the four unsupported-claim cases carried expected_status='grounded' together with supports_claim=false. That label recorded what the defective engine did, not what should happen, so fixing the engine made status_correct disagree with the stale label. v2 sets expected_status='insufficient_evidence' for those four. v1 is left byte-identical so the original numbers stay reproducible.
